title: Sweet Potato Buttermilk Pull-Apart Rolls
changes_from_base: Mashed sweet potato and buttermilk enrich a 15-roll dough baked in a rectangular tin.
summary: Soft, orange-tinged pull-apart rolls made with mashed sweet potato and tangy buttermilk.
equipment: large bowl or stand mixer with dough hook
cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: orange-fleshed sweet potato, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

steps.title: Sweet potato
steps.text: Simmer the sweet potato in unsalted water 10-13 min, until very soft. Drain well, mash in a large bowl, then beat in the buttermilk and 55 g butter until fairly smooth.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Add the flour, yeast, sugar, eggs and salt and mix, then knead 8 min by machine on medium-low (or by hand on a lightly floured worktop), until smooth, elastic and slightly sticky.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Put the dough in a buttered bowl, cover and leave about 1 1/2 h in a warm place, until more than doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Butter the tin. Turn out the dough, divide it into 15 pieces and roll each into a smooth ball. Set them in the tin in 3 rows of 5, cover and leave 45 min, until they fill the tin.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Brush with half the melted butter and bake 22-26 min, until deep orange-gold; the centre roll reads 88-90 °C.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Brush with the remaining butter as they come out and cool 10 min before pulling apart.

tips: Drain the sweet potato well so the dough is not too wet.
If the dough is very sticky, add flour a spoonful at a time.
Brush with butter twice for a soft, shiny top.
storage: Keep cooled rolls in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. Rewarm at 180 °C for 5 min; freeze for up to 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
